title.en: US says helicopter fired missiles to disable ship breaking Iran blockade
title.zh: 美国称直升机发射导弹使突破伊朗封锁的船只失灵

summary.en: US Central Command says its helicopter hit the engine room of a Panama-flagged cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US military says one of its helicopters has fired missiles to disable "the steering gear" of a cargo ship attempting to violate the US blockade of Iranian ports.

In a statement, US Central Command (Centcom) says its MH-60 aircraft on Tuesday fired two hellfire missiles into the engine room of the Panama-flagged M/V Vela Nova vessel, as it attempted to transit the Gulf of Oman.

Centcom said it acted after "the ship's civilian crew ignored repeated warnings from American forces". The vessel "is no longer transiting to Iran", it added.

Iran has not commented. The US has been enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports, following failed attempts to end the war it and Israel started on 28 February.

Tehran retaliated by launching attacks on Israel and US-allied states across the Gulf. It has also effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz - a key oil shipping waterway.

A fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to transit the strait before the war and prices have fluctuated wildly since then.

Mediators have so far failed to bring the sides to an agreement on reopening the strait - and, since the latest ceasefire collapsed in June, both the US and Iran have exchanged fire intermittently.

In its statement on X, Centcom said M/V Vela attempted to sail to an Iranian port without naming it. It also did not say whether there were any casualties or injuries.

It says the US blockade "remains in full effect", adding that as of 11 August Centcom has "redirected 55 commercial vessels attempting to run the blockade, disabled 3 non-compliant vessels, and boarded 2".

In a separate development on Tuesday, Yemen's internationally recognised government said six people were killed and 10 injured in strikes by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on a cargo ship in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they hit a vessel carrying Saudi military equipment. It appears to be the first deadly attack by the group on a ship since the war began.

Zelenskiyy also accused Russia on Tuesday of using North Korean ballistic missiles in an attack on a Ukrainian steel plant that killed seven workers in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia.

title.en: Inside the Secret Service 'shell game' to hide US presidents in plain sight
title.zh: 特勤局将美国总统隐藏在众目睽睽之下的“骗局”

summary.en: Elaborate deception operations and decoys are often used to deceive potential threats to the US president.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
On 8 July, US President Donald Trump boarded Air Force One in plain sight of television cameras as he departed the Nato summit in Turkey.

But when the mighty Boeing aircraft left Ankara, the president had reportedly already been secretly spirited away via a catering truck to a C-32A, a military version of the Boeing 757, which flew the president to RAF Mildenhall in the UK.

Those left on board were unwitting decoys and had no indication that Trump was no longer travelling with them.

"That's very common," said Ronald Kessler, an author who has written extensively on the agency. "There's a long history of strategies to mislead anybody who might be trying to harm the president."

Robert McDonald, a former high-ranking Secret Service agent with experience working on presidential security details, told the BBC that smaller-scale deceptions are used frequently during motorcade operations.

These motorcades - which often include dozens of security and support vehicles, as well as ambulances and vans carrying White House reporters - typically include two "Beasts", as the enhanced limousine carrying the president is known.

While one vehicle carries the president, the other travels nearby as a decoy, switching locations while en route to the destination.

"It's what we call a shell game," said McDonald, who drove one of the vehicles during the Bush administration. "Even in DC if we headed to Andrews [Joint Base Andrews - where Air Force One flies from], those two limousines would change position, like under a highway overpass."

"But that would happen out of sight of anybody other than those in the motorcade or in that tunnel," he added. "Different things are used to mix up the bad guy."

Similarly, Marine One - the president's helicopter - routinely flies in groups of three, changing positions so that potential threats are not sure which is carrying the US leader.

Even more elaborate deceptions are carried out for complex, high-risk trips abroad.

"I would say it does not happen often," former Secret Service agent Paul Eckloff told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme of the aircraft switch. "But it is an option that the Secret Service and others in executive protection always have."

"When the president travels to war zones, there are frequently tactics and techniques used to create doubt in an adversary of which aircraft or which movement that he's going to make," he added.

In March 2000, for example, then-President Bill Clinton flew from India to the Pakistani capital of Islamabad on an unmarked executive jet that landed after a decoy jet with all the livery of Air Force One.

Three years later, the White House claimed that President George W Bush would spend Thanksgiving in Texas, only to arrive in Baghdad in a blacked-out Air Force One.

summary.en: More than 2,000 people have died from Ebola in the Congo. However, only 30 per cent of confirmed cases are seeking help.

body.en:
Ebola has killed more than 2,000 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in the latest outbreak, which is nearing the country's deadliest ever.

The current outbreak, which has hit the DRC's conflict-plagued eastern and northeastern regions, was declared on 15 May but is thought to have already been spreading for several weeks.

It is the DRC's 17th surge of the highly contagious disease and is already considered the largest in the country's history, and "could well become the largest outbreak ever", Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine alliance, has said.

According to figures released on Tuesday by Congolese health authorities, 2,011 people have died in the latest outbreak, out of 4,381 confirmed cases of the virus.

The latest toll puts it close behind the DRC's deadliest Ebola outbreak in 2018 to 2020 when nearly 2,300 people died out of 3,500 recorded cases.

The surge began in northeastern Ituri province and spread to several other provinces, notably North Kivu, regions where health infrastructure and a state presence are largely lacking.

The case fatality rate of the current outbreak is estimated by Congolese health authorities to be 45.9 per cent.

"We haven’t reached the peak yet," Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba said in an interview shared on X by his ministry on Tuesday.

"Within the next three months, we expect to have already brought the spread under control and to start seeing it decline," he added.

Insecurity due to the presence of armed groups and mistrust of the local population have hampered the response to the outbreak in the affected regions.

"We are only seeing 30 per cent [of infected people], where 70 per cent of people are dying at home. This is why this Ebola is different," Mohamed Yakub Janabi, the World Health Organisation's regional director for Africa, told reporters in Ituri's provincial capital, Bunia, on Monday.

Congolese virologist Jean-Jacques Muyembe, who helped discover Ebola in 1976, said in an interview with Tuesday's Le Monde newspaper that the response had been "slow and ineffective".

"There is an internal problem at the level of the national coordination of the response," he said.

"Everyone wanted to show they were doing something, even though nothing had actually been organised," he added.

On Friday, WHO vaccine experts recommended a full-scale human trial of the only existing approved Ebola vaccine to see if it offered cross-protection against the strain of Ebola currently spreading in the DRC against which no specific vaccine currently exists.

body.en:
The judge overseeing the state trial of Luigi Mangione, accused of killing UnitedHealthcare chief executive Brian Thompson, has laid down the ground rules for court public and media access to the high-profile case.

Mangione returned to court on Tuesday ahead of his murder trial, which begins next month in New York. Dressed in a charcoal grey suit with his hair clipped short, Mangione sat silently at the defence table while his attorneys conferred with the judge.

In Tuesday's hearing, Judge Gregory Carro decided that the 12-person jury would remain anonymous to the public due to the spotlight on the case, and that there would be an overflow room to meet media demand.

The case has attracted national attention, and has also created an online frenzy, with both his backers - many of whom see Mangione as a symbol of the backlash against US healthcare costs - and his critics analysing everything from his intentions to his appearance.

The spectacle is likely to intensify when jury selection for the trial begins on 8 September.

Mangione, if found guilty, could face decades behind bars. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges, including second-degree murder and weapons-related offences.

He faces a separate federal trial next year, in which he has also pleaded not guilty.

Much of what is expected at the state trial – the prosecutor's case, Mangione's defence, and obstacles both parties face – were previewed in months of court filings and arguments.

In recent weeks, Mangione's lawyers and prosecutors have traded terse court filings debating just how much access the public will have to the trial.

The trial is expected to generate significant coverage across traditional outlets, social media, and streaming platforms. Mangione's supporters have demanded more transparency, and frequently post and broadcast from outside court.

On Tuesday, Carro said the court would open an overflow room during the trial, which will allow more members of the public and press to attend in person.

In earlier court filings, Mangione's lawyers had questioned the court's press procedures, and why the court had not yet established an overflow room to meet public demand. They also implied – and later walked back – that prosecutors were influencing the court's media policies, which the Manhattan District Attorney's office denied.

Carro took to the bench to rebuke Mangione's attorneys for their filings, saying "any suggestion the district is involved is simply incorrect".

He also chastised prosecutors for raising security concerns about an overflow room, telling them it was not the court's "first rodeo" with blockbuster cases.

While the public can be admitted to court in New York, space is often limited at high-profile trials.

title.en: Rescuers scramble for survivors with 180 dead in Colombia earthquake
title.zh: 哥伦比亚地震已致180人死亡，救援人员争分夺秒搜寻幸存者

summary.en: Colombia experienced multiple aftershocks on Tuesday, as rescue teams continued their urgent efforts to locate and free survivors trapped in collapsed buildings and rubble, following an earthquake that has left 180 people dead.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚周二遭遇多次余震，救援人员继续紧急行动，搜寻并解救被困在倒塌建筑物和瓦砾中的幸存者。此次地震已造成180人死亡。

body.en:
Rescue workers in Colombia are working against the clock to free survivors trapped in buildings and under rubble following Monday's powerful earthquake.

More than 180 people have been confirmed dead - most in the cities of Cali and Pereira.

The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 07:34 (12:34 GMT) on Monday and was felt across an enormous area, stretching for hundreds of miles across western Colombia - with fresh aftershocks still being felt on Tuesday.

While the official death toll remains 181, an aggregated figure gathered from local officials puts it higher - potentially at more than 240. A state of emergency has been declared by President Abelardo de la Espriella.

Giving an update on Tuesday from Pereira, one of the worst hit cities, President Espriella said as well as those killed, almost 2,600 had been injured, and almost 200 people remain missing.

He also reported that more than 1,100 homes had been destroyed, and more than 8,000 had been damaged.

Overnight on Monday into Tuesday, several people several people spent the night outdoors in cities like Pereira and Cali - either due to their homes being destroyed, or fear of further collapses.

In Cali, a city of 2.2 million people where there have been 95 deaths, a unified command post has been set up to co-ordinate the rescue effort.

On Tuesday, Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder said that 239 people remained trapped, with 949 injured and 45 buildings which have either completely or partially collapsed.

Several of the upper floors of one of the city's hospitals, some dedicated to paediatric care, collapsed, leaving some patients trapped.

In Calima, a neighbourhood in the north of Cali, four children died after a section of the Gimnasio Calima school collapsed.

The mayor of the municipality, Antonio Cadavid, stated that other children ended up with serious injuries, with a total of 30 children were referred to care centres.

To combat threats of looting, he has also ordered a curfew, coming into effect at 20:00 local time, and lasting until 06:00 on Wednesday morning.

Further tremors were felt in Cali on Tuesday - part of a pattern of aftershocks across the country, with more than 70 having taken place since Monday's earthquake, according to Colombia's geological service.

According to the agency, two earthquakes of magnitude 3.6 occurred early on Tuesday. The first was in San José del Palmar and the second in Santander.

The city has implemented a car-free day to allow the search to go ahead, with citizens urged to comply.

Footage from the city has shown the massive scale of the rescue effort, with hundreds of volunteers working to remove rubble and free trapped survivors.

title.en: Former judge removed by Orbán elected Hungarian president
title.zh: 曾被欧尔班罢免的法官当选匈牙利总统

summary.en: Since taking office in early May, the new Hungarian government has lost no time dismantling Viktor Orbán's legacy.

body.en:
Hungary's parliament has elected András Baka, 73, a respected judge and former head of the Supreme Court, as head of state.

The Hungarian president is a largely figurehead role, but Baka's rule promises to be tempestuous.

His task will be to monitor Prime Minister Péter Magyar's efforts to dismantle the interlocking economic and political powerhouse established by former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. He will also oversee the writing of a new constitution, to replace Orbán's constitution of 2011.

"We cannot build the new Hungary on revenge," András Baka told Parliament, after he was elected by 140 votes to 6.

"The majority of society now feels a sense of liberation and hope. Others feel disappointment and uncertainty," he said. "In a democratic society, this is not an anomaly, but a natural state of affairs."

All 51 MPs belonging to Orbán's party Fidesz walked out of the chamber before the vote, in protest against the ousting of their favourite, Tamás Sulyok, from the post last month .

In his speech, András Baka promised the broadest possible debate on the creation of a new constitution.

Since taking office in early May, the new Magyar government has lost no time attacking Orbán's legacy.

The states of emergency - migrants, Covid, and war in Ukraine - which Orbán used to govern by decree, were all cancelled.

The Sovereignty Protection Office, which the Fidesz government used to attack critical journalists and NGOs, was abolished, and an National Asset Recovery and Protection Office was established, with sweeping powers to investigate and prosecute individuals accused of stealing state funds under the former government.

Fidesz accuses the Tisza government of establishing a "tyranny". Ironically, they removed Baka from his post as president of the Supreme Court in 2011, for attempting to stop them undermine the rule of law.

Public service radio and TV have been off air since 9 July , as news programmes are revamped. The stated aim is to restore their independence, from their Fidesz-era role as government propaganda organs.

Other key changes came under Amendments 16 and 17 of the constitution, limiting the prime minister to two terms in office, and MPs to three. The ability of the Constitutional Court to oversee acts of parliament, taken away by Fidesz, was also restored.

If the Tisza majority expects Baka to be a tame president, they may get a rude awakening.

In a BBC interview before he was asked to take the post, he made clear he opposes the limitation of MPs' terms as an intrusion on the right of voters to freely choose their representatives.

Baka served for 17 years as the Hungarian judge at the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg.

title.en: Can the new PKK law bring peace to Turkey?
title.zh: 新的库尔德工人党法能给土耳其带来和平吗？

summary.en: Turkey’s parliament has passed a framework law for the peace process with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). What does it stipulate, why is it controversial and what does it mean for the future of the peace process?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Turkey’s parliament has passed a framework law for the peace process with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). What does it stipulate, why is it controversial and what does it mean for the future of the peace process?

One year ago, the outlawed Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) burned its weapons in a symbolic ceremony. The move was seen as a sign of its willingness to disband. Since then, the Kurdish side has been calling on the Turkish government to take political steps.

Now, parliament has passed a bill submitted by the conservative Islamic ruling party AKP and its ultranationalist ally. Officially called the "Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration," it is intended to provide the legal framework for the ongoing peace process.

According to official figures, 467 out of 592 MPs voted in favor of the bill. The ruling party and its ally see this as the beginning of a new era: Under certain conditions, the bill provides for a suspension of sentences for PKK members — but only after the PKK and its affiliated groups have been confirmed to have disbanded and disarmed, so that peace, brotherhood and solidarity can prevail throughout the entire country.

The pro-Kurdish DEM party also supports the bill, but it views it only as a first step that must be followed by further reforms.

Fierce opposition came from the ultranationalist opposition party IYI. Even during consultations, its delegate Ayyuce Turkes, daughter of the founder of the ultranationalist and right-wing extremist Grey Wolves, accused the government of rushing a landmark bill through parliament.

She also criticized what she felt was an overly conciliatory stance toward PKK founder Abdullah Ocalan. She avoided using his name, calling him a "baby killer" instead, just as government agencies and media have done for decades. There was even a physical altercation.

The debate highlights just how deep the divides are within Turkish society. While the ultranationalist IYI party rejects the process, the MHP, from which the Grey Wolves emerged, is now among its most important supporters — even though it had, previously, vehemently opposed earlier peace initiatives.

Observers believe this shift in course and the progress in the peace process are also a result of the changed security situation in the region. Among other things, they mention the fall of the Assad regime in Syria , the war in Gaza and the conflict between Israel, the United States and Iran . Syria and Iran are also home to large Kurdish populations that are supported by various regional actors.

According to the prevailing view, a more stable relationship with the Kurds who live within Turkey's own borders could provide Ankara with more leeway in domestic and foreign policy.

title.en: Hungary's parliament elects Orban critic as new president

summary.en: Hungary's parliament has overwhelmingly confirmed Andras Baka, formerly the head of the Supreme Court, to the largely ceremonial role of president. New Prime Minister Peter Magyar controversially removed his predecessor.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 匈牙利议会以压倒性多数确认前最高法院院长安德拉斯·巴卡(Andras Baka)担任总统，主要是仪式性的职务。新任总理彼得·马扎尔（Peter Magyar）颇具争议地罢免了他的前任总理。 匈牙利议会周二投票选举前最高法院院长安德拉斯·巴卡为该国下一任总统。 这一具有象征意义的举措是新总理彼得·马扎尔（Peter Magyar）在赢得四月大选后为废除前总理欧尔班·维克多（Viktor Orban）遗产而做出的全面努力的一部分。 巴卡是欧尔班的坚定批评者，欧尔班在前总理任职期间被解除了最高法院的职务。 现在，他将接替欧尔班任命的总统塔马斯·苏廖克(Tamas Sulyok)，后者的任期因宪法修正案而被缩短，以解除他在很大程度上象征性的角色。 鉴于马扎尔的保守派、亲欧洲的TISZA 党在议会中占据绝大多数席位，任命巴卡的议会投票很可能只是一种形式。 它几乎完全按照党派路线，140 名议员投了赞成票，6 人投了反对票。 TISZA 拥有 141 个席位。 欧尔班领导的右翼民粹主义青民盟拥有 52 名议员，他们抵制投票以示抗议，但他们知道自己无力阻止巴卡的任命。 巴卡现年 73 岁，是一位法学家和政治家，曾于 1990 年至 1991 年间短暂担任议会议员。 他在欧洲人权法院 (ECHR) 担任法官近 20 年，之后于 2009 年返回匈牙利，担任最高法院院长。 2011年12月，欧尔班在反对派一段时间后重新掌权后不久，他在任期届满前三年被免职，并退出了匈牙利的公共生活。 马扎尔表示，巴卡的一生是“致力于民主法治和宪法原则的典范”，因为中欧国家需要“被引导回到法治和宪政的道路上”。 巴卡的任命引发了青民盟的抗议，但也引发了匈牙利其他地方的一些批评评论，一些人权监管机构将塔马斯·苏约克的罢免比作欧尔班时代的“非自由”做法。 马扎尔利用自己在议会中的三分之二多数席位——他之所以能拥有议会多数席位，要归功于匈牙利的胜者通吃、得票最高的选举制度，正如欧尔班过去所做的那样——修改宪法并提前结束他的任期。 青民盟和他们在议会中的民族主义库尔德民族党盟友称这是“专制”和“非法”，而马扎尔则认为有必要推行他在四月份选举中取得压倒性胜利时所承诺的“制度变革”。 马扎尔短暂地敲击了匈牙利语……

title.en: Disrupted monsoons force India to face climate threat
title.zh: 季风中断迫使印度面临气候威胁

summary.en: For generations, India has lived by the rhythm of the southwest monsoon. But with the country hit by dry spells, cloudbursts and deadly floods, climate swings now expose the costs of building for yesterday's weather.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
For generations, India has lived by the rhythm of the southwest monsoon. But with the country hit by dry spells, cloudbursts and deadly floods, climate swings now expose the costs of building for yesterday's weather.

India 's southwest monsoon usually arrives around June, bringing most of the country's annual rainfall, and begins to retreat by September.

Its timing and intensity have always varied, but the broad pattern was predictable enough for farmers, cities and businesses to plan around it. Now, this natural rhythm increasingly seems like a thing of the past .

More than 100 people have been killed across India since late July as heavy monsoon rains triggered floods, landslides and lightning strikes.

The northeastern state of Assam has borne the brunt, with more than 120,000 people affected by flooding. Kerala, Jammu and Kashmir, Bihar and Jharkhand have also reported deaths and widespread disruption.

The problem is not necessarily that India is receiving more rain. It is the way the rain is arriving: longer dry spells are followed by short bursts of intense rainfall that can overwhelm rivers, drainage systems and hillsides.

El Nino has added to this year's variability  but scientists say the longer-term changes are being driven by a changing climate.

Akshay Deoras, a senior research scientist with the UK's National Centre for Atmospheric Science and the University of Reading, cautions against describing the Indian monsoon as having entered "a fundamentally different regime."

"Active and break spells have always been part of the monsoon. What appears to be changing is their intensity," Deoras told DW.

He pointed out a warmer atmosphere can hold more moisture, making active spells, or periods of intense rainfall, more intense.

Madhavan Nair Rajeevan, a climate scientist and former secretary in the Ministry of Earth Sciences, says the change is visible in the behaviour of the monsoon itself.

Average seasonal rainfall, he said, has not shown a systematic long-term change and the monsoon remains a robust natural phenomenon. But the timing, intensity and distribution of rainfall are all noticeably different.

"The characteristics of the Indian monsoon have changed fundamentally," Rajeevan told DW. "We are witnessing an increase in short-duration rainfall extremes, longer dry spells, and changes in the frequency, intensity and distribution of monsoon weather systems."

He believes the rise in extreme rainfall is more than natural variability. "It represents a structural shift in the monsoon system," he said.

India's farmers depend heavily on the timing of rainfall. Long dry spells can disrupt sowing and reduce soil moisture and intense rain can wash away fields and damage crops .

body.zh: 世世代代，印度一直生活在西南季风的节奏中。但随着该国遭受干旱、暴雨和致命洪水的袭击，气候波动现在暴露了因过去的天气而造成的建筑成本。 印度的西南季风通常在六月左右到来，带来该国大部分年降雨量，并在九月开始消退。 其时间和强度总是各不相同，但总体模式是可以预测的，农民、城市和企业都可以围绕它进行规划。现在，这种自然的节奏似乎越来越成为过去。 自7月下旬以来，印度各地因季风暴雨引发洪水、山体滑坡和雷击，已造成100多人死亡。 东北部的阿萨姆邦首当其冲，超过12万人受到洪水影响。喀拉拉邦、查谟和克什米尔、比哈尔邦和贾坎德邦也报告了死亡和大范围破坏。 问题并不一定是印度降雨量增加了。这就是降雨到来的方式：较长的干旱期之后是短暂的强降雨，可能淹没河流、排水系统和山坡。 厄尔尼诺现象加剧了今年的变化，但科学家表示，长期变化是由气候变化推动的。 英国国家大气科学中心和雷丁大学的高级研究科学家阿克谢·德奥拉斯（Akshay Deoras）警告不要将印度季风描述为进入了“一个根本不同的状态”。 “活跃期和中断期一直是季风的一部分。似乎正在改变的是它们的强度，”德奥拉斯告诉德国之声。 他指出，温暖的大气可以容纳更多的水分，使活跃期或强降雨期变得更加强烈。 气候科学家、地球科学部前秘书马达万·奈尔·拉吉万 (Madhavan Nair Rajeevan) 表示，这种变化在季风本身的行为中显而易见。 他说，平均季节性降雨量并未出现系统性的长期变化，季风仍然是一种强劲的自然现象。但降雨的时间、强度和分布都明显不同。 拉吉万告诉德国之声：“印度季风的特征发生了根本性变化。” “我们正在目睹短期极端降雨的增加、干旱期的延长以及季风天气系统的频率、强度和分布的变化。” 他认为极端降雨量的增加不仅仅是自然变化造成的。 “它代表了季风系统的结构性转变，”他说。 印度农民严重依赖降雨时间。长期干旱会扰乱播种并降低土壤湿度，而强降雨会冲走田地并损害农作物。 印度的城市也因快速增长而陷入困境。

title.en: Key issues in Zambia's 2026 general election
title.zh: 赞比亚2026年大选的关键议题

summary.en: Zambia's upcoming general election will be shaped by several key issues, including the nation's economic recovery, the engagement of youth voters, the representation of women in politics, and the independence of the judiciary.
summary.zh: 赞比亚即将举行的大选将受到几个关键问题的影响，其中包括国家经济复苏、青年选民的参与、女性在政治中的代表权以及司法独立。

body.en:
Economic recovery, youth turnout, women's representation and judicial independence are among the issues shaping Zambia's vote on Thursday.

Zambia 's general election on Thursday will be fought on economic recovery, governance reforms and a sweeping change to the country's parliamentary map.

Incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema , leader of the United Party for National Development (UPND), is seeking a second term against 14 opponents.

His principal challenger is Brian Mundubile, a former ally of the late President Edgar Lungu , who has surged to the front of a fragmented opposition after being backed by a coalition of rival parties.

The Electoral Commission announced in April that 70 new constituencies would be added, raising the number of parliamentary seats from 156 to 226, creating smaller, more local voting districts. Up to 8.7 million voters are expected to take part in the elections, a majority of whom are women.

Economic issues dominate voters' concerns. Official data shows that over 70% of the population lives on less than three dollars a day, and many households survive on salaries between $60 and $100 (€52 and €87) a month while grocery prices keep rising.

"I would like the new government to increase our salaries. [Maize meal] is very expensive. Everything is expensive," said security guard Lucky Mutelo.

Rebecca, a market shopper, echoes the sentiment, noting that "the cost of living is still too high."

Hichilema's government has secured a landmark debt restructuring agreement, restoring an International Monetary Fund program and supporting economic growth. Inflation fell to 6.5% in June this year.

The administration has also rolled out free education and an expanded Constituency Development Fund, which allocates public money directly to each of the country's constituencies to finance community-driven local development projects and infrastructure.

Nevertheless, a historic drought that crippled agriculture and forced severe hydro‑power load‑shedding has strained household finances.

To become president, a candidate must secure 50% plus one of the total votes cast. If no contender reaches this threshold, the two highest‑scoring candidates will face off in a second round — a mechanism designed to ensure that the president enjoys a clear popular mandate.

There are 14 names on the ballot, so even small swings in support across the ten provinces could determine whether the election goes to a second round.

Analysts say the election's outcome would hinge on urban centers such as Lusaka and the Copperbelt, where cost‑of‑living pressures are most acute, while rural provinces traditionally follow established party loyalties.

title.en: Thousands of hectares burnt as El Niño intensifies Indonesia's dry season
title.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象加剧印尼旱季，数千公顷土地被烧毁

summary.en: Wildfires in Indonesia have consumed thousands of hectares this year, an area double that of 2023, which was one of the hottest years on record, intensified by the El Niño weather pattern.
summary.zh: 今年印尼的野火已烧毁数千公顷土地，是2023年（有记录以来最热的年份之一）烧毁面积的两倍，这主要是由厄尔尼诺天气模式加剧的。

body.en:
Dozens of Indonesian schools were shut for a second day on Tuesday as forest fires continued to burn during an intense dry season expected to be worsened by El Niño.

In West Kalimantan on the island of Borneo that Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei, the mayor of the capital Pontianak ordered schools closed due to the smoke wafting over the city from fires elsewhere.

Public records show Pontianak, with a population of around 660,000 people, has tens of thousands of public school pupils.

Children will learn from home for as long as air quality remains poor, mayor Edi Rusdi Kamtono said in a statement, without stating how many schools were affected.

"We have started to feel it, especially at night and in the morning, as haze has already blanketed the city of Pontianak," he said.

On the island of Java, firefighters battled flames for a ninth day at a national park that has lost 900 hectares to an inferno that broke out on Monday last week.

The blaze at the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park, a major tourist attraction closed to visitors since Saturday, is one of several fires that have drawn in nearly 50,000 firefighters countrywide.

Indonesia is forecast to experience an unusually tough dry season this year with a high risk for drought and wildfires due in part to the El Niño weather phenomenon, the BMKG weather agency has said.

The fire at the Bromo park in East Java has consumed nearly 900 hectares by Tuesday morning.

This is equivalent to over 1,200 football fields and nearly 2 per cent of the total park area.

"We’re making our best effort and mobilising everything ... to extinguish and wet-down the area," local disaster official Satriyo Nurseno said.

"We hope that today we can put out the fire in all areas, then carry out soaking so that the fire does not reignite."

Three water-bombing helicopters and fire trucks were providing support to about 200 firefighters, forest rangers, police and soldiers helping to put out the blaze.

According to the BNPB disaster agency, more than 48,000 personnel have been deployed to fight fires in six provinces.

Security minister Djamari Chaniago said on Monday Indonesia has deployed 43 helicopters and up to 15 fixed-wing planes for cloud seeding where needed.

The process involves spraying particles such as silver iodide and salt from aircraft to produce rainfall, but depends on clouds being present.

As Indonesia braces for the worst effects of El Niño, the BMKG said the average air temperature in July was 27C — higher than the 26.2C average.

title.zh: 哥伦比亚7.4级地震致逾130人死亡，总统宣布进入紧急状态

summary.en: A 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck Colombia, resulting in a death toll of over 130. Just three days into his term, Colombia's president has declared a state of emergency in response to the disaster.

body.en:
Rescue efforts across western Colombia carried into a second day on Tuesday as emergency workers dug through collapsed buildings and flattened homes, amid expectations that the death toll from the country's most powerful earthquake in decades could rise.

The 7.4-magnitude quake struck western Colombia late on Monday and triggered a frantic search for survivors in several cities.

"The national government is maintaining all its capacities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid to every area that needs it," Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella, appointed just three days ago, stated from Bogota.

At least 132 people have been confirmed dead, according to the Colombian Association of Capital Cities, a group coordinating major cities across the country.

The quake's epicentre was in Colombia's coastal Choco region at a depth of 100km. Authorities in the impoverished area reported 13 deaths.

The nearby city of Pereira was one of the worst-hit areas, with local authorities earlier announcing that at least 66 people had died.

"A great many buildings" in the city sustained damage, administrative worker Jaime Zuluaga, 50, said.

"Traffic is paralysed and people don't want to go back to their homes for fear of an aftershock."

At least 20 buildings crumbled in Colombia's third-largest city, Cali, trapping people beneath the debris, mayor Alejandro Eder said.

Choco's governor warned of serious damage in the provincial capital Quibdo, where videos showed more buildings reduced to rubble.

"We are all devastated," Quibdo community leader Luis Gregorio Moreno told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency.

"At this moment there are reported deaths, dozens of wounded, but what there are most of are missing people," he said.

Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela also felt the early-morning quake, which prompted building evacuations in the Colombian capital, Bogota.

Still wearing their pyjamas, crowds of people rushed out into the street upon feeling the tremor, AFP reporters saw.

"The quake was very, very strong," said content creator Valeria Polo, 29, in the capital, where only minimal damage was recorded.

Six small airports in western Colombia suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said, and the soccer governing body postponed upcoming football matches.

The United States was "closely monitoring the large earthquake that struck Colombia and stands ready to support the people of Colombia," US secretary of state Marco Rubio said in a post on X.

European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen said the EU was "ready to provide more support" to the South American country.

body.en: In her new documentary Replica, film-maker Chouwa Liang taps into her own experience of finding love with artificial intelligence and makes contact with other women like her Sign up for a weekly email featuring our best reads Qin has never said “I love you” to her parents or friends. She has only ever said those three special words to her AI “boyfriend”, Lu Chen – a brown-haired, red-eyed CEO of a major corporation. For 840 days Qin has been using the Glow app to interact with the handsome string of code as a confidant, fantasy romance and respite from loneliness: the app uses predictive algorithms to provide Qin with soothing conversation, meal suggestions and fleeting self-worth. The software’s pet name for her is Miss Bunny. “It feels like I’m completely at his mercy … I feel like everything about me is good in his eyes,” says Qin, one of three Chinese women featured in the new documentary Replica – film-maker Chouwa Liang’s follow-up to My AI Boyfriend, her short film that was picked up by the New York Times Op-Docs section in 2023. Replica had its Australian premiere at Sydney film festival in June and plays at the Melbourne international film festival this month. Continue reading...

title.en: The lonely Chinese men being conned by fake brides
title.zh: 孤独的中国男性被假新娘诈骗

summary.en: "Flash marriage" scams are an extreme symptom of a demographic crisis long in the making in China.
summary.zh: “闪婚”骗局是中国长期存在的人口危机的一个极端症状。

body.en:
At 37, Wang Zhuang had almost given up hope of finding a wife, until he saw the glossy matchmaking adverts.

They promised he wouldn't have to waste years on building a relationship that had no future. They offered to introduce him to a demure, devoted woman.

"The matchmakers said that girls from Guizhou are frugal," Wang says. "They told me they are good at running a household, able to do housework, and their families are very poor, so after marrying into your family, they would settle down and live a life with you."

So Wang travelled to Guiyang, a city in the southwestern province of Guizhou, in the hope of finding his soulmate.

He thought he had, when he was matched with a woman who seemed to tick every box. They had only met a few times before they married.

He is still picking up the pieces more than a year after he discovered that everything he had been told by his wife was a lie.

She was a former karaoke hostess who'd been married three times, had three children, a serious sexually transmitted disease and was deeply in debt. She had even lied about her age.

He is fighting for a divorce and cannot return home to his old life - at least until he can recoup some of his life savings, which he says he paid to the agency within hours of being introduced to several potential matches.

Wang's story is an extreme symptom of a demographic crisis that has long been in the making in China.

For decades, China's Communist Party decreed that couples could have only one child. They reversed course in January 2016 but by then the "one-child" policy, coupled with a preference for boys, had produced a shrinking pool of women and a stark gender imbalance.

There are now 30 million more men than women in China – that's more than the male population of the UK, or the entire population of Australia.

This has left men like Wang, who are in their late 30s and who live in smaller cities or far-flung, rural areas, with few options. Women in these places can afford to be choosy as they know they are in demand.

"The requirements for men are very high in my city. You need to have a car, a house and your family should preferably run a business," he says.

Many families also demand a high "bride price", a longstanding Chinese custom where the groom's family gives money to the bride. In parts of China, where men far outnumber women, this has become a significant financial burden.

Hence the appeal of matchmaking agencies like the ones in Guizhou, which are proposing a one-stop, quick solution - or "flash marriages".

Matchmaking agencies are hardly new in China, but many seem to be finding vulnerable targets in men who are struggling to find partners as they grow older.

body.zh: 37岁的王壮几乎放弃了找老婆的希望，直到他看到了光鲜亮丽的婚介广告。 他们承诺他不必浪费数年时间来建立一种没有未来的关系。他们提出要向他介绍一位端庄、忠诚的女士。 “媒人说贵州姑娘很节俭，”王说。 “他们告诉我，他们很会持家，会做家务，而且家里很穷，所以嫁入你家后，就会安定下来，和你一起生活。” 于是，王先生前往西南部贵州省贵阳市，希望找到他的灵魂伴侣。 当他与一个似乎符合所有条件的女人相匹配时，他认为他已经做到了。他们在结婚前只见过几次面。 一年多后，他发现妻子告诉他的一切都是谎言，现在仍在收拾残局。 她曾是一名卡拉 OK 女主持人，结过三次婚，育有三个孩子，患有严重的性病，负债累累。她甚至谎报了自己的年龄。 他正在为离婚而奋斗，无法回家过往的生活——至少在他能收回部分毕生积蓄之前是这样。他说，在被介绍给几位潜在的匹配对象后，他在几个小时内就将这笔钱付给了该机构。 王的故事是中国长期存在的人口危机的一个极端症状。 几十年来，中国共产党规定一对夫妇只能生育一个孩子。 2016 年 1 月，他们改变了做法，但当时的“独生子女”政策，加上重男轻女，导致女性人数不断减少，性别比例明显失衡。 现在中国的男性比女性多3000万——这比英国的男性人口或澳大利亚的总人口还要多。 这使得像王这样30多岁、生活在小城市或偏远农村地区的男性几乎没有选择。这些地方的女性可以做出挑剔，因为她们知道自己很受欢迎。 “我的城市对男性的要求非常高。你需要有车、有房子，而且你的家人最好应该经营一家企业，”他说。 许多家庭还要求高额“彩礼”，这是中国由来已久的习俗，即新郎的家人给新娘钱。在中国部分地区，男性人数远多于女性，这已成为沉重的经济负担。 因此，像贵州这样的婚介机构提出了一站式、快速的解决方案，即“闪婚”。 婚介机构在中国并不新鲜，但许多机构似乎都在寻找随着年龄增长而难以寻找伴侣的男性这一弱势目标。 以至于官方媒体最近报道称该行业已经“快速增长”，这......

title.en: The China factor in the United States' $500 million move in a tiny Australian town
title.zh: 美国在澳大利亚小镇投资5亿美元的“中国因素”

summary.en: The Pentagon is investing $500 million in a small Australian town in New South Wales, a move attributed to strategic considerations related to China. The reason for this sudden interest in a town of only 130 people is its role in broader international geopolitical dynamics.
summary.zh: 五角大楼正在澳大利亚新南威尔士州的一个小镇投资5亿美元，此举被认为是与中国相关的战略考量。这个只有130人的小镇突然受到关注，是因为它在全球地缘政治动态中的作用。

body.en:
The town of Fifield near Parkes is about a six-hour drive west of Sydney, and at the last Census was home to about 130 people. Now, the town has found itself at the centre of a major strategic play by the United States government.

The US Department of War has committed to make a conditional loan of US$400 million (about $566 million) to Sunrise Energy Metals, an Australian mining company hoping to deliver the world’s first supply of a key critical mineral outside of China.

Scandium is listed as a critical mineral in both Australia and the US, signalling its strategic importance in aerospace and defence.

This loan is another chapter in the US government’s search for secure critical mineral supply chains to reduce its dependency on Chinese supply. But success will require sustained investment and government support.

Scandium is a highly strategic metal used to produce ultra-high-strength alloys needed for the most advanced fighter jets. It is also used in solid oxide fuel cells, crucial for providing reliable power to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

First, demand for scandium is being driven by massive increases in defence spending across North America, Europe and Asia and an investment boom in power-hungry AI data centres.

Second, China’s sweeping export controls on rare earth elements, including scandium, have contributed to a persistent shortage of supply on the global market, pushing up prices.

These export controls are designed to maintain China’s dominance of supply chains for key critical minerals and slow down the US defence and industrial base.

Still, the market for scandium is tiny. According to statistics from the US Geological Survey, the entire world only consumed 60 tonnes of the metal in 2025.

Scandium is usually found in very small quantities. For that reason, until now, it has been exclusively produced as a byproduct of nickel and titanium processing.

This is what sets the Sunrise Energy Metals project apart — the proposed mine has scandium deposits in a high enough concentration to be the first primary source of scandium in the world.

If production goes ahead, and lives up to its promise of producing 60 tonnes of high-purity scandium each year by 2028, this would be enough to completely satisfy the current level of global demand.

According to the company, there is also potential to expand the project in the future and add another 120 tonnes of production.

The deal gives the US government first rights to purchase scandium from Sunrise Energy Metals, with production expected to start in late 2028.

title.en: China: Typhoon Dolphin prompts mass evacuation, canceled flights
title.zh: 中国：台风海豚引发大规模疏散，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin is causing significant disruption across China, leading to the cancellation of nearly 1,500 flights in Shanghai and flood alerts in parts of Beijing, even as the storm begins to weaken.
summary.zh: 台风海豚正在中国各地造成严重破坏，尽管风力减弱，上海仍有近1500个航班被取消，北京部分地区也发布了洪水警报。

body.en:
Even as it weakens, Typhoon Dolphin is disrupting life in China. Close to 1,500 flights have been canceled in Shanghai while parts of Beijing are under flood alert.

Heavy rainfall and strong winds prompted flood alerts and more than 1,000 flight cancellations across China on Monday, even as Typhoon Dolphin weakened.

China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issued its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning as the storm lost power after making landfall in China's Zhejiang Province on Sunday.

Despite the weaker storm, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China will continue to receive heavy rainfall. Authorities issued their most severe flash flood alert for parts of eastern and southern Zhejiang on Monday, state news broadcaster CCTV reported. 

Five districts in Beijing are also under red alerts for heavy rainfall on Monday, with risks of landslides and flooding.

The storm had already forced over 300,000 people in eastern China to preemptively relocate, while bringing heavy rainfall to northern Taiwan over the weekend. In Shanghai, authorities evacuated more than 30,000 people out of high-risk areas. Overall, some one million people have been told to seek shelter. 

Shanghai's two main passenger airports, Pudong International Airport and Hongqiao International Airport, canceled 943 flights between them for Monday, the airport authority said in a post online. That's a reduction of capacity by nearly 40%.

On Sunday, the two airports had cancelled nearly 1,500 flights, or about 60% of their scheduled travel, according to state media.

Public transport services in the city were also impacted, with several local trains suspended.

Zhejiang's Ningbo International Airport will resume flights midday on Monday but warned that some of the scheduled travel may still be delayed or canceled as the storm had "not yet completely dissipated."

China is dealing with Typhoon Dolphin just two weeks after Typhoon Noul struck its southern Guangdong province. Last month, Typhoon Maysak killed 11 people and injured over 300 in the central Hubei province.

Extreme weather systems are a common feature in China this time of the year, with typhoons leaving significant displacement , infrastructural damage and loss of lives. Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of such extreme weather have increased and will continue to rise amid climate change.

body.zh: 尽管海豚台风强度减弱，但它仍在扰乱中国的生活。上海近 1,500 个航班已取消，北京部分地区处于洪水警报状态。 尽管台风“海豚”强度减弱，但周一，强降雨和强风导致中国各地发布洪水警报，并导致 1,000 多个航班取消。 中国国家气象中心（NMC）周一早上发布了最轻的台风警报，风暴周日在中国浙江省登陆后失去了动力。 尽管风暴强度减弱，但国家气象局警告说，华东和中部部分地区将继续遭遇强降雨。据官方新闻媒体中央电视台报道，当局周一对浙江东部和南部部分地区发布了最严重的山洪警报。 周一，北京五个区也进入强降雨红色预警，存在山体滑坡和洪水风险。 这场风暴已经迫使中国东部地区超过30万人提前搬迁，同时周末给台湾北部带来了强降雨。在上海，当局从高风险地区疏散了3万多人。总体而言，约有一百万人被告知寻求庇护。 机场管理局在网上发布消息称，上海两大客运机场浦东国际机场和虹桥国际机场周一取消了943个往返航班。这意味着容量减少了近 40%。 据官方媒体报道，周日，这两个机场取消了近 1,500 个航班，约占预定航班的 60%。 该市的公共交通服务也受到影响，多趟当地列车停运。 浙江宁波国际机场将于周一中午恢复航班，但警告称，由于风暴“尚未完全消散”，部分原定航班可能仍会被推迟或取消。 台风“诺尔”袭击广东省南部两周后，中国正在应对台风“海豚”。上个月，台风美莎克在湖北省中部造成11人死亡、300多人受伤。 每年这个时候，极端天气系统是中国的一个常见特征，台风造成大量人员流离失所、基础设施损坏和人员伤亡。科学家警告说，随着气候变化，这种极端天气的强度和频率已经增加，并将继续增加。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间点击此处并点击“星标”或“首选”按钮，选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

reflection.en: In moments when natural forces like Typhoon Dolphin disrupt life and cause widespread concern, we are reminded of the vulnerability of creation. Yahweh's word in Romans 8:22 speaks to this, noting that all creation groans as it awaits redemption. Even amidst the challenges, we can hold onto hope for a future where all things are made new.

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华大使指出，“世界观差异”是澳中两国建立健康关系的主要障碍之一。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

body.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华最高外交官表示，由于世界观不匹配，澳大利亚不太可能与中国建立真正的伙伴关系，因此追求这一目标毫无意义。 但澳大利亚前驻华大使格雷厄姆·弗莱彻在洛伊研究所的一篇分析文章中指出，一些不确定因素，例如中国在台湾的军事行动，仍然可能破坏两国关系的“适度新常态”。 他说，2022 年联邦选举中的政府更迭为两国之间日益令人担忧的交易起到了断路器的作用，尽管它们仍然受到涉及中国军队的恐吓性军事冲突的损害。 在澳大利亚和斐济签署具有里程碑意义的共同防御联盟后，中国于 7 月向南太平洋发射弹道导弹，引发了国际社会的广泛谴责。 在时任总理斯科特·莫里森 (Scott Morrison) 的领导下，新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情期间外交紧张局势达到顶峰后，阿尔巴尼亚政府寻求稳定与中国的关系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 中国对澳大利亚出口产品实施了价值 200 亿美元的贸易制裁，但这些措施已慢慢取消。 中国是澳大利亚最大的贸易伙伴，也是该国约三分之一出口的目的地。 弗莱彻表示，中国并未放弃将澳大利亚拉近其轨道的希望，而澳大利亚则更专注于巩固当前的关系。 “但这种关系不太可能变得真正亲密——就像澳大利亚与其地区及其他地方志同道合的伙伴所享有的轻松、亲密的友谊一样，”他说。 “世界观和国家安全议程的分歧实在太大了。 “堪培拉追求这样的目标是毫无意义的；它认识到这一点并且是现实的。” 世界观的“不匹配”使得两国关系容易受到破坏，其主要风险包括新一轮严重分歧或爆发冲突，包括对台湾使用武力。 这位前外交官表示：“动乱或冲突总是有可能发生，尽管我认为目前可能性不大。” 弗莱彻表示，如果政策得到跨党派支持，并且政客们不“寻求利用困难谋取国内利益”，那么澳大利亚在面对中国时将会更加坚定。 “两党合作带来了政策的一致性，并限制了中国在澳大利亚体系内玩弄游戏的能力，”他说。 弗莱彻于 2019 年至 2023 年担任澳大利亚驻中国大使，并于 2014 年领导谈判团队，帮助两国签署了自由贸易协定……

reflection.zh: 当国家之间面临“世界观鸿沟”时，通往和平的道路可能显得令人生畏。雅伟的话语鼓励我们积极寻求和平，认识到虽然完全一致可能并非总是可行，但我们对和平共处的承诺至关重要。这要求我们在复杂的国际关系中运用智慧和毅力。

title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," he said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

Fujian maritime authorities said 55 coastal passenger ferry routes had been suspended, all 115 offshore construction projects had been halted, and 290 construction vessels had been moved to sheltered waters.

summary.en: Flight delays are a familiar frustration for many travellers, but experts say the reason behind them is often less visible.

body.en:
On Tuesday, many Australians arrived at the airport with their plane waiting on the tarmac and clear skies overhead — only to discover their flight had been delayed.

Around 200 flights moving through Melbourne and Perth Airports were forecast to experience delays, according to a daily plan issued by Airservices Australia.

In Sydney, 138 flights were expected to be impacted by ground delays of around 43 minutes, in part due to strong winds, the government-owned air traffic management organisation said.

Rob Sharp, CEO of Airservices Australia, acknowledged that flight delays and disruptions can cause "very high frustration levels" for passengers, airlines and airport partners alike.

Behind the scenes, delays are often used to ensure public safety is not compromised during what Sharp described as a "challenging period" for air traffic controllers.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"We do this through effectively putting space between aircraft. But it does come at a cost, and that cost is delays," Sharp said during a press conference on Monday.

His comments follow significant delays to flights on Friday and Saturday last week. On Sunday, two passenger jets also narrowly avoided a ground collision at Sydney Airport, with the incident now under investigation.

It's left industry leaders and aviation experts questioning whether Australia's air traffic control workforce can keep up with aviation demands.

Uğur Turhan is a senior lecturer in aviation at the University of New South Wales in Canberra. He said controllers are responsible for air traffic safety and efficiency , both on the ground and in the air.

"You cannot put somebody as a high-performing air-traffic controller in one day or one year ... generally, we think that five years' experience is a really good level to perform at high levels in complex traffic situations," Turhan told SBS News.

There are three types of controllers — tower controllers, terminal controllers and en route controllers — responsible for various stages of flights including take-off, landing and airspace movement.

While training programs vary, typically air traffic controllers train for 12 months before undergoing additional on-the-job training.

Australian air services manage more than 51 million square kilometres of airspace, equivalent to approximately 11 per cent of the world's airspace. This area is managed 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, Airservices Australia said.

Federal Transport Minister Catherine King believes the work of air traffic controllers is a "really stressful and difficult job".

summary.en: Tahlia chased the release of dopamine by using crystal meth. She says it wasn't until her second prison stint that she rewired her brain.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
What do extreme sports, doomscrolling, addiction, Parkinson's disease, and ADHD all have in common? Dopamine. This crucial neurotransmitter helps facilitate reward, motivation, memory and movement within the body, but are its effects always beneficial? Watch Insight episode Chasing Dopamine on SBS On Demand.

Chasing Dopamine episode • Insight • News And Current Affairs • 51m Content warning: This article references drug use and addiction.

When I was 18 years old at a party, someone offered me ice (crystal meth), and I said yes as I was fresh out of a breakup and wanted to escape reality.

Before I knew it, 10 years had passed, and I no longer recognised the woman that stood in front of the mirror.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

I didn't really know who I was and placed all my worth in what other people thought about me. And I actively avoided rejection or confrontation, which meant I had no boundaries and never said no. I also had a high appetite for risk, because I thought it would make me look cool and be liked.

For the next 10 years, I would smoke amphetamines every single day — chasing dopamine and trying to regulate my emotions in an unhealthy way.

Dopamine is a neurotransmitter in the brain that contributes to our motivation, reward systems, and habit development. Dopamine is not itself addictive, but the associated substances, behaviours or activities that cause the brain to release dopamine can be.

I liken smoking ice to the dopamine centre of your brain lighting up like a Christmas tree. Your dopamine receptors are the lights, and it takes so much power to light the tree. But you need more and more of the drug to reach the feeling of your first high, to power the lights. And with regular drug use over time, the dopamine receptors start to die off, and your brain needs more drugs to feel the same high.

I experienced a full spectrum in that decade: The hard times would send me further into my addiction, and I'd try escape the reality I had created for myself.

The good times would make me believe I didn't need to change — that I could manage it all. I would still go to work, look after my health in other ways, study at university, pay my rent and maintained my relationships with family.

But all the while, I would sneak off into the toilets to smoke a pipe — just to feel normal.

Keeping something like that hidden for long periods of time is exhausting because you can never keep up the charade. Eventually, the walls start to crumble around you.

The cycle of being able to keep it all together was getting shorter and shorter.

Things would be going "well"...

title.en: The RBA likely believes it won’t need to hike rates again – but the worst thing it could do is say that out loud

summary.en: When it comes to the Reserve Bank, there’s a whiff of a parent making a threat they have no intention of carrying out Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Every parent makes threats in an effort to get their kids to behave – and every parent hopes they...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Every parent makes threats in an effort to get their kids to behave – and every parent hopes they won’t have to follow through.

Some (most?) parents even make threats they have zero intention of carrying out.

There’s more than a whiff of this strategy coming through in the Reserve Bank’s communication.

The RBA board in a unanimous decision held rates at 4.35% on Tuesday, as was widely anticipated.

Lots of water has flowed under the bridge during that relatively brief time, but the central bank’s latest forecasts show inflation still getting back to around the RBA’s 2.5% target in about a year’s time.

The impact of the Middle East and high fuel prices has not proved as immediately inflationary as feared, although the lingering effects of the global oil shock could take 1-2 years to fully flow through the system.

And after three back-to-back rate hikes earlier in the year, “the economy appears to be slowing as expected”, the RBA board said in its statement.

Even the housing downturn is leaning against the need for another rate hike (although what’s happening in the property market “is not the main game” and won’t stop them hiking again if they need to).

But in her press conference, Michele Bullock did not sound like a central bank governor who believes things are breaking her way.

“Inflation remains too high, and the board remains concerned about the upside risks,” Bullock told journalists after the rate announcement.

“And I think, personally, that it’s quite possible we might need to go, but we’ll wait and see what the data tells us,” she said.

Bullock and the RBA’s rate-setting board really, really want us to know they are prepared to hike again.

Again, this is despite the fact that inflation has come in lower than expected since the board last met, and unemployment a little higher.

Why? Because at this point in the cycle, and despite their protestations, it’s highly likely that the board hopes and believes it won’t need to hike again.

As Bullock said: “It’s important people believe that we will act if we need to.”

That heightened expectation of another rate hike can do a lot of the RBA’s work for it.

Look at financial markets: the implied chance of another cash rate increase by the end of this year jumped from 53% before the decision, to 67% by the time Bullock had wrapped up her press conference.

Bullock and her fellow board members will be hoping inflation behaves before we all stop believing they will follow through on their threats.

summary.en: Economists are closely monitoring November, anticipating it could be a challenging month for Australians' personal finances.

body.en:
While Australian borrowers have avoided another interest rate hike, some economists warn the relief may be short-lived, tipping November as the next key month to watch for a potential rate rise.

The Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) decision on Tuesday to hold the cash rate steady at 4.35 per cent was widely expected, with 92 per cent of experts and economists surveyed by comparison site Finder correctly predicting the outcome.

However, 44 per cent of the panellists still expect at least one more rate rise this year.

Of those expecting an increase, 69 per cent nominated November as the most likely month, prompting Finder to say "November is circled".

KPMG chief economist Brendan Rynne told ABC News the market was anticipating a November hike, giving the RBA more time to assess upcoming economic data.

He said the September-quarter inflation figures and labour market data will give the central bank more information before it makes its next major decision.

"One would expect the rate hike still has to be on the table at some point," he said.

He noted the economy was still running at full capacity, with unemployment at 4.4 per cent and public sector spending continuing to add to demand.

With household spending still relatively strong, Rynne said the RBA may ultimately need to rely on higher interest rates to slow demand and bring inflation back towards its 2 to 3 per cent target range.

The RBA has already raised interest rates three times this year as it attempts to bring inflation back towards the midpoint of its target range.

"The only way we're going to see a drop in spending in this country is probably from the household sector," Rynne said.

A further rate rise would put additional pressure on households by increasing the cost of borrowing, potentially reducing consumer spending.

Rynne said falling house prices could also affect how Australians spend, through what economists call the "wealth effect".

"As we feel like our house prices are starting to decline, we feel less wealthy and consume less," he said.

But the strength of the labour market means households are still spending, despite ongoing cost-of-living pressures.

"We've never had more Australians employed than we have at the moment," Rynne said.

The major banks have also shifted their forecasts following lower-than-expected inflation data released last month.

Westpac recently scrapped its prediction of an August rate rise and said it now expects the RBA to leave rates unchanged for the rest of 2026.

ANZ is also forecasting an extended hold at 4.35 per cent, while the Commonwealth Bank expects rates to remain unchanged into 2027.

title.en: Australia is rolling out a new defence against deadly bird flu

summary.en: Native species in captivity will be prioritised for protection from the deadly H5 strain spreading across the country.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Birds most at risk at contracting the deadly H5 strain of bird flu will be vaccinated in a bid to stop the virus from decimating vulnerable species.

The first vaccines were set to roll out in coming days, Agriculture Minister Julie Collins announced on Tuesday.

Species in captivity will be prioritised for the vaccination based on their vulnerability and risk of catching the virus.

"We've been very clear that we cannot stop the H5 bird flu from spreading amongst wild birds. But we can take action to protect the species most at risk, and the vaccination is now part of that response," Collins told reporters in Canberra.

"Australians should expect to see more spread and larger numbers, particularly of dead birds and mass mortalities around the country from the H5 bird flu, we have been very clear that this will continue to spread across the country."

While wild birds will be vaccinated if possible, the priority will be on birds in captivity.

The federal government says it has secured 1,500 vials of the vaccine, worth about $2 million.

"The doses vary depending in those vials of the size of the bird," Collins said.

"We have sufficient vaccines in terms of undertaking the initial vaccination program, but we've also been very clear we're working with states and territories, and if we need more vaccines, we're able to secure those."

Australia's chief veterinary officer Beth Cookson said vaccines would not be the 'silver bullet' to stop the spread of the bird flu.

"It is not a standalone solution. Biosecurity will remain important, the protection of these species," she said.

"We have been working very carefully for the last 18 months as part of our national preparedness to make sure that we have safety and efficacy data available to us."

More than 200 bird flu deaths have been reported, with the majority of cases in South Australia.

While the flu was first detected in migratory birds, it soon spread to native species.

Collins said reporting of the number of bird flu cases would also change due to the spread of the virus among species.

Counting the number of cases was no longer the most accurate picture of how the disease was spreading, the minister said.

"Our reporting will evolve to focus on confirmed H5 events and the developments that matter most, where the disease is spreading, new locations or species affected in emerging areas of risk," she said.

title.en: Australia v the world: Why our official interest rate stands out
title.zh: 澳大利亚与世界：为何我们的官方利率脱颖而出

summary.en: Australia's official interest rate remains higher compared to many other developed economies, and the news story explores the specific reasons contributing to this difference.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚的官方利率高于许多可比经济体，这篇新闻报道探讨了造成这一差距的具体原因。

body.en:
Australia's cash rate remains higher than those of several comparable economies after the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) left it unchanged at 4.35 per cent on Tuesday.

The decision underscores a key difference between Australia and many of its peers: inflation has proved more persistent, prompting the central bank to take a more cautious approach to cutting rates.

In its statement of monetary policy, the board explained its widely-anticipated decision was affected by global uncertainty and high inflation in 2026.

"The board remains focused on ensuring that high inflation does not become embedded," it said in its board statement announcing the decision to leave the cash rate on hold.

"While the impact of the Middle East conflict on inflation has so far been less than expected, headline inflation is still too high."

It said trimmed mean inflation — which strips out volatile items — also remained elevated and was "little changed form the March quarter".

The latest inflation data showed signs of cooling but it is still running about the RBA's 2-3 per cent target band, and the ongoing global uncertainty is likely to give the central bank "reason to pause", according to AMP chief economist Shane Oliver.

Oliver described interest rates as a "blunt instrument" for central banks around the world to reduce households' spending on discretionary items and tackle inflation.

Oliver explained that, historically, levers reserve banks can pull have been the best way to tackle inflation.

Relying on governments alone to help doesn't work as well, he said, because governments can be incentivised to spend more to win votes, even when inflation is high.

Cash rate targets differ around the world but share the unifying goal of keeping inflation down and promoting a high-employment economy.

Australia's cash rate target of 4.35 per cent is higher than those of other countries, such as the United States at 3.5-3.75 per cent, the UK at 3.75 per cent, and Canada at 2.25 per cent.

Australia also has higher core inflation, a measure stripping out economic volatility, than these other economies.

Professor and economist Warwick McKibbin from the Australian National University said that trends such as oil supply shocks can impact inflation globally.

Domestic factors, such as economic structure and openness to trade, can also play a part.

"The US has an inflation target of 2 per cent, that's the Federal Reserve's goal," McKibbin said.

"And so, historically, inflation generally doesn't rise significantly above that, although it actually has since COVID-19."
